title: Last week’s Microsoft Outlook outage turned a hotel pool fault into a hospital trip for 15 guests
summary: A pool safety alert at a German hotel was sent by email, but the email never arrived.
body: TL;DR Fifteen guests at a hotel in Germany were reportedly hurt after a faulty dosing system pumped too much chlorine into the hotel pool. The pool’s safety system sent a warning by email, but staff never received it because of last week’s global Microsoft 365 outage. Microsoft says the outage was caused by a problem from an earlier network capacity upgrade, and it has promised a full post-incident report. Last week’s Microsoft 365 outage did more than keep people out of their inboxes. In Germany it played a part in a chemical incident that sent hotel guests to the hospital. German public broadcaster WDR reported that on Friday, November 13, a fault in the automatic chlorine dosing system at Hotel Ling Bao pushed far too much chlorine into the hotel’s pool. The hotel belongs to the Phantasialand theme park in Brühl, near Cologne.

title: How to tell if a Black Friday deal is actually worth it
summary: After years of hunting Black Friday deals, here's the key to separating the bargains from the bluster.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority I’ve spent the best part of a decade hunting down deals for Android Authority , and I learned very quickly that a big discount doesn’t necessarily mean you’re getting a bargain. Black Friday is a particularly good time to remember this, with retailers plastering huge percentage discounts over everything in sight. Contrary to the memes, some are genuinely excellent deals — I can assure you that some tech devices will hit their lowest price ever this month. But you’ll also see many ‘Black Friday deal’ labels on discounts at a price higher than three months ago. Thankfully, there’s a very easy way to tell the difference. The key to assessing a Black Friday deal is to use a price tracker. These tools let you see what a product has cost over recent months or even years, so you can judge for yourself whether that 50% discount is really worth getting excited about. They’re so easy to use that it’ll barely be slowing your shopping spree down at all once you’re in the rhythm. I’ll walk you through it here.

title: OpenAI rolls out ChatGPT Wallet to let Dots AI agents make purchases
summary: Wallet is available to US-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers.
body: TL;DR OpenAI launches ChatGPT Wallet to let its Dots AI agents make purchases for users. Wallet is available to US-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers who have a US-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express. The move comes as some retailers and service providers ban AI agents from their platforms. OpenAI’s Dots personal AI agents are gaining the ability to shop, with the launch of ChatGPT Wallet today. The digital wallet substitutes a payment token for a user’s credit card details and lets its Dot make purchases. ChatGPT Wallet is available to US-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers who have a US-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express card. OpenAI said that while Dots will assist in the purchase process, users will review the items, be apprised of the total, select the card to use, and approve the purchase with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan. The goal, though, is for the agents to ultimately have more control.

title: Recompa simplifies Android handheld installs so you can spend more time playing
summary: Recompa aims to make your life easier by simplifying Android handheld installs.
body: Credit: Nathan Lohnes TL;DR Recompa is an app that finds and installs decompilations and native ports that work with Android devices and handhelds. The app provides a more seamless way to search for and install games and apps than looking through GitHub. While it’s designed for handhelds, it also works with phones and tablets. Now that all colors of the Retroid Pocket Duo are shipping , it’s time to start thinking about the games you’ll put on it. While GitHub has thousands of decompilations to choose from, finding and downloading the files you want can be a burdensome task. If you’re not all that familiar with using GitHub, there’s something you can use to make searching for and installing games on your Android handheld much easier. That’s where the Android app known as Recompa comes into play. This app is designed to simplify the sourcing and installation of decompilations and native ports. Recompa organizes these decompilations and ports as if they were in a marketplace, making the act of searching for and exploring games far easier. When you find the title you’re looking for, you can install it with the press of a button.
